articles.title: Understanding the CBK Base Rate and How It Affects Your Loans
articles.excerpt: The Central Bank Rate (CBR) is the rate at which the Central Bank of Kenya lends to commercial banks. Learn how changes in CBR directly impact your personal loan and mortgage repayments.
articles.author: MoneyIQ Team

content.text: The Central Bank Rate (CBR) — often called the base rate or benchmark rate — is one of the most important numbers in Kenya's financial ecosystem. Set by the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK), it determines the cost at which commercial banks borrow money from the central bank.
What is the CBK Base Rate?

The CBR is a monetary policy tool used by the Central Bank of Kenya to control inflation and stabilize the economy. When the CBK raises the base rate, borrowing becomes more expensive. When it lowers the rate, borrowing becomes cheaper.
As of early 2026, the CBK base rate stands at 10.00%, though this can change at any Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, held approximately every two months.
How Does the CBR Affect Your Loans?

Commercial banks use the CBR as a reference point when setting their own lending rates. While banks add their own margin (risk premium) on top of the CBR, any change in the base rate typically flows through to consumer loan products:

items: Personal Loans: A 1% increase in CBR can add KES 500-2,000 to your monthly repayment on a KES 1 million loan.
Mortgages: Since mortgages have longer tenures (15-25 years), even small rate changes have a massive impact on total interest paid.
Business Loans: Higher rates increase the cost of capital for businesses, which can slow economic growth.
Car Loans: Vehicle financing costs also track the CBR, affecting your monthly auto loan payments.

content.text: What Should Borrowers Do?

If you're planning to take a loan, timing matters. When the CBR is trending downward, it may be worth waiting for lower rates. Conversely, if rates are rising, locking in a fixed-rate loan sooner rather than later can save you money.
Use our Mortgage Calculator or Personal Loan Calculator to see exactly how rate changes affect your monthly payments.
Historical Context

The CBR has varied significantly over the years. It peaked at 18% in 2012 during a period of high inflation and has generally trended downward since then, with periods of adjustment. Understanding this history helps put current rates in perspective.

The key takeaway: the CBK base rate is the foundation of all lending rates in Kenya. By following MPC decisions and understanding their implications, you can make better-informed borrowing and saving decisions.

articles.title: Best Mortgage Rates in Kenya 2026: Complete Guide
articles.excerpt: Compare mortgage rates from all major Kenyan banks and find the best home loan deal. We break down rates, fees, and requirements for first-time homebuyers.
articles.author: MoneyIQ Team

content.text: Buying a home is likely the biggest financial decision you'll ever make. In Kenya, where property prices continue to rise — especially in Nairobi, Mombasa, and satellite towns like Kiambu and Machakos — choosing the right mortgage can save you millions of shillings over the life of your loan.
Current Mortgage Rates (2026)
Mortgage rates in Kenya currently range from 12% to 15% per annum, depending on the bank, your employment status, loan amount, and property location. Here's a snapshot of rates from major banks:

items: Standard Chartered: 12.00% — Best for high-net-worth individuals
ABSA Bank Kenya: 12.50% — Competitive for salaried employees
Stanbic Bank: 12.80% — Good terms for self-employed
Equity Bank: 13.00% — Accessible for first-time buyers
KCB Group: 13.50% — Strong nationwide branch network

content.text: What Affects Your Mortgage Rate?

items: Employment status: Salaried employees with check-off typically get lower rates than self-employed applicants.
Deposit amount: A higher deposit (20-30%) can reduce your rate by 0.5-1%.
Property type: New developments from approved developers may qualify for preferential rates.
Loan amount: Larger loans (above KES 10M) may attract better negotiated rates.
Relationship banking: Existing customers with salary accounts often get preferential terms.

content.text: Tips for First-Time Homebuyers

If you're a first-time homebuyer in Kenya, start by getting pre-approved from 2-3 banks before shopping for property. This gives you negotiating power and a clear budget. Also factor in additional costs: legal fees (1-2%), stamp duty (2-4%), valuation fees, and insurance.
Use our Mortgage Calculator to compare monthly payments across different banks and see how much you can afford.
Remember, the lowest interest rate isn't always the best deal. Compare total costs including fees, insurance requirements, and early repayment penalties before making your decision.

articles.title: Money Market Funds in Kenya: Earn More Than Your Savings Account
articles.excerpt: Money Market Funds offer higher returns than traditional savings accounts with easy access to your money. Here's how to choose the right MMF in Kenya.
articles.author: MoneyIQ Team

content.text: If your money is sitting in a traditional savings account earning 2-4% per year, you're essentially losing money to inflation. Money Market Funds (MMFs) offer a smarter alternative, with returns typically ranging from 8% to 14% per annum — while still keeping your money accessible.
What is a Money Market Fund?

A Money Market Fund is a type of unit trust (mutual fund) that invests in short-term, low-risk financial instruments like Treasury bills, corporate bonds, and fixed deposits. They're regulated by the Capital Markets Authority (CMA) in Kenya.
Top MMFs in Kenya

items: CIC Money Market Fund: ~13% annual return, minimum KES 1,000
Cytonn Money Market Fund: ~12% annual return, minimum KES 1,000
Sanlam Money Market Fund: ~11% annual return
ICEA Lion Money Market Fund: ~10% annual return
Britam Money Market Fund: ~10% annual return

content.text: MMF vs Savings Account vs Fixed Deposit

The key advantage of MMFs over savings accounts is significantly higher returns. Unlike fixed deposits, MMFs offer liquidity — you can typically withdraw your money within 1-3 business days. This makes them ideal for emergency funds, short-term savings goals, and parking cash between investments.
Use our Savings Calculator to see how much more you'd earn with an MMF compared to a savings account.

While MMFs are considered low-risk, they're not risk-free. Returns are not guaranteed and can fluctuate. However, they remain one of the best options for Kenyans looking to grow their savings without locking away their money.

articles.title: HELB Loan Repayment: Everything You Need to Know in 2026
articles.excerpt: A comprehensive guide to understanding your HELB loan repayment schedule, penalties, and how to clear your balance faster.
articles.author: MoneyIQ Team

content.text: If you attended university in Kenya, chances are you have a HELB (Higher Education Loans Board) loan. With over 2 million Kenyans owing HELB money, understanding your repayment options is crucial for your financial health.
HELB Loan Basics

HELB charges a 4% annual interest rate on the outstanding loan balance. Repayment begins one year after completing your studies. The standard monthly deduction for employed individuals ranges from KES 1,500 to KES 5,000, depending on your salary.
Repayment Options

items: Employer deduction (check-off): The most common method. Your employer deducts the HELB repayment from your salary automatically.
Direct payment: You can make payments directly via M-Pesa (Paybill 200800) or bank transfer.
Lump sum: You can make a one-time payment to clear your balance at any time.
Salary deduction notice: If your employer isn't deducting, apply for a compliance certificate.

content.text: What Happens If You Default?

Defaulting on your HELB loan has serious consequences: a 10% penalty on the outstanding balance, CRB (Credit Reference Bureau) listing which affects your ability to access bank loans, potential legal action, and denial of HELB clearance certificates needed for some employers.
Use our HELB Calculator to see exactly when you'll be debt-free and how increasing your monthly payment can save you thousands in interest.
The best strategy is to pay more than the minimum required amount. Even an extra KES 1,000-2,000 per month can significantly reduce your total interest and cut years off your repayment period.

articles.title: Fixed Deposit vs Money Market Fund: Which is Better for Your Savings?
articles.excerpt: Should you lock your money in a fixed deposit or invest in a money market fund? We compare returns, liquidity, risk, and tax implications.
articles.author: MoneyIQ Team

content.text: When you have money to save or invest in Kenya, two of the most popular options are fixed deposits and money market funds (MMFs). Both are considered relatively safe, but they differ significantly in returns, liquidity, and suitability.
Fixed Deposits Explained

A fixed deposit is a bank product where you lock away a lump sum for a set period (typically 1-12 months or longer) at a fixed interest rate. Rates range from 5% to 9% depending on the bank and tenure. The longer you lock, the higher the rate.
Money Market Funds Explained
MMFs pool money from many investors and invest in short-term government and corporate securities. They offer returns of 8-14% and allow withdrawals within 1-3 days. There's no lock-in period.
Head-to-Head Comparison

items: Returns: MMFs typically offer higher returns (8-14%) than fixed deposits (5-9%).
Liquidity: MMFs win — you can access your money in 1-3 days. Fixed deposits lock your money for the agreed term.
Minimum investment: MMFs start as low as KES 1,000. Fixed deposits typically require KES 50,000-100,000.
Risk: Both are low-risk. Fixed deposits have deposit insurance (KDIC covers up to KES 500,000). MMFs are regulated by CMA.
Tax: Both are subject to withholding tax on interest/dividends (15% for residents).

content.text: Our Savings Calculator can show you the difference in returns between a fixed deposit at 7% and an MMF at 11% over any time period.
Our recommendation: Use MMFs for your emergency fund and short-term goals. Use fixed deposits when you need a guaranteed rate and can afford to lock away a larger sum for 6-12 months or longer.
